column1: Example of Finney's new measures in a boomtown
column2: In the winter of 1830–1831 Finney preached frequently in Rochester, the nation's first inland boomtown, using protracted meetings, the anxious bench, and public testimony to systematically promote conversion.

Average yearly consumption of distilled liquor fell from over five gallons per American over age 15 by 1825, the highest level in American history, to below two gallons by 1845 after the American Temperance Society and about 5,000 local societies campaigned against drink.

The 1836 Maria Monk book, a lurid invented account of convent life, outsold every book except Uncle Tom's Cabin before the Civil War, a Charlestown mob burned a convent in 1834, and Philadelphia riots in 1844 left 14 people dead.

In the Divinity School Address of July 1838, Emerson asked how many pulpits made man sensible "that he is an infinite Soul," and he later advised, "Trust thyself. Every heart vibrates to that iron string."

column1: Example of Thoreau's experiment at Walden
column2: In 1845 Thoreau built a cabin on Walden Pond and lived there for 16 months to demonstrate self-reliance, later writing that Americans trapped by property and the market led "lives of quiet desperation."

column1: Example of why Brook Farm failed
column2: George Ripley organized Brook Farm so members could live more simply than under competitive institutions, but Romantic individualists such as Margaret Fuller and Nathaniel Hawthorne could not sustain the group cooperation the community needed.

column1: Example of a secular utopian failure
column2: Robert Owen's New Harmony, Indiana, attracted about 900 volunteers and dissolved in 1827, and the book notes that wages were too high and land too cheap for most Americans to join such communities.

column1: Example of religious communitarian life among the Shakers
column2: Following Ann Lee, Shakers practiced celibacy, separated the sexes in work and living, and split church leadership equally between men and women, peaking at about 6,000 members before declining for lack of natural increase.

column1: Example of Mormon growth and persecution
column2: Joseph Smith's followers built Nauvoo, Illinois, to a population of 10,000 by the mid-1840s, but after Smith was murdered in 1844 they left in 1846, and Brigham Young led them to Utah in 1847.

On January 1, 1831, Garrison's Liberator rejected gradual emancipation, embraced immediatism, denounced colonization, and later he burned a copy of the Constitution after condemning it as "a covenant with death and an agreement with hell."

column1: Example of violent opposition to abolitionists
column2: A Boston mob seized Garrison in 1835, and Elijah Lovejoy was murdered in Alton, Illinois, in 1837, evidence of the bitter resistance abolitionism met even in the North.

column1: Example of the jump from abolition to women's rights
column2: After being seated behind a curtain at a London antislavery convention, Stanton and Mott organized Seneca Falls in 1848, where about a hundred supporters issued a Declaration of Sentiments beginning, "All men and women are created equal."

column1: Example of the gag rule's unintended effect
column2: When the House in 1836 automatically tabled antislavery petitions, abolitionists could defend white civil liberties as well as attack slavery, broadening their appeal until the rule was repealed in 1844.

column1: Example of women gaining public skills through benevolence
column2: Benevolent and reform societies gave women the practical experience of holding office, conducting meetings, drafting policy statements, organizing programs, and raising money, so evangelicalism enabled them to enter public life even under the cult of domesticity.
